faqs.q: What is the difference between Hajj and Umrah?
faqs.a: Hajj is the obligatory pilgrimage every able Muslim must perform once in a lifetime, on specific days of Dhu'l-Hijjah (Hajj 2027 falls 14–19 May 2027). Umrah is non-obligatory and can be performed any time of year. From Pakistan, Umrah trips typically last 10–14 days; Hajj trips run 25–40 days because of the multi-stage rites at Makkah, Mina, Arafat, Muzdalifah, and Madinah.

faqs.q: What documents do I need?
faqs.a: Valid passport (6+ months from return date), recent passport-size photographs, NIC copy, Meningococcal ACYW135 vaccination certificate (mandatory for Hajj, recommended for Umrah), Polio vaccination certificate within last 6 weeks (mandatory for Pakistanis travelling to Saudi). For minors: birth certificate plus father's consent letter if mother travels alone with children. For couples: marriage certificate may be required for some package categories.

faqs.q: How early should I book Hajj 2027?
faqs.a: As early as possible. Pakistan's Hajj visa quota from Saudi (~179,000 seats annually, split between the Government Hajj Scheme and licensed Private Hajj Operators) fills months in advance. Premium hotels near Masjid al-Haram book out 6+ months ahead. For Hajj 2027 (mid-May 2027), confirm your booking by November–December 2026 at the latest.

faqs.q: How early should I book Umrah?
faqs.a: For standard Umrah, 2–4 weeks before travel is comfortable. Ramadan Umrah (busiest period) needs 6–8 weeks ahead because flights, hotels near the Haram, and visa slots are all in peak demand. Off-peak months (mid-September to mid-October, late February to early April) are easiest to book on short notice.

faqs.q: Are payment plans available?
faqs.a: Yes — for Hajj packages we accept staged payments (typically: confirmation deposit on booking, balance due before visa submission). For Umrah, full payment is usually required before ticket issuance because international airfares and hotel pre-pays do not allow staged structures. Your Regional Representative will walk you through specific options on the first call.

faqs.q: Can my elderly parents travel?
faqs.a: Yes. We arrange airport wheelchair assistance in Jeddah and Madinah, hotels closer to the Haram for those with mobility issues, slower-paced Ziyarat tours, and ground transport with assistance. Tell us your family's needs and we'll tailor the package — this is one of our most common arrangements.

faqs.q: Are family Umrah packages available?
faqs.a: Yes. We tailor hotel categories, room types (connecting rooms, large suites for 4–6 people), and Ziyarat pacing for families of any size — couples, parents with adult children, multi-generational groups. Tell your Regional Representative the group composition and we'll quote accordingly.

faqs.q: What is the Nusuk platform?
faqs.a: Nusuk is the Saudi government's official platform for Hajj and Umrah pilgrim management — visa issuance, Masjid al-Haram and Riyadh-ul-Jannah entry permits, and trip planning. We handle all Nusuk-related steps on your behalf; you do not need to register or operate the platform yourself, though you can install the Nusuk app to track your visa and entry permits.

faqs.q: What hotels do you book?
faqs.a: It depends on package tier. Economy: 3-star or 4-star hotels in the Misfalah area (800m–2km from Haram) — common chains include Al Olayan, Dar Al Eiman, Anjum. Premium: 4–5 star hotels in Ajyad / Abraj Al Bait towers area (50–300m from Haram) — including Hilton Suites, Anjum, Conrad, Pullman Zamzam. Hotel selection is confirmed at booking; substitutions only if a specific hotel is fully sold out.

faqs.q: Which countries do you handle student visas for?
faqs.a: UK, USA, Canada, Australia primarily, plus Germany, France, Ireland, New Zealand, and Malaysia as commonly requested. Tell us your university acceptance and destination and we will confirm what is needed for that specific country.

faqs.q: How long does the application take?
faqs.a: UK Student Route: 3 weeks standard, 5 working days priority. USA F-1: depends mostly on interview wait time — currently very long in Pakistan for new applicants (often 6–12 months at the Karachi/Islamabad consulates), so apply 8+ months before your intake. Canada Study Permit via SDS: 20 calendar days target. Australia subclass 500: 4–8 weeks typical. Always start early.

faqs.q: Do you guarantee visa approval?
faqs.a: No agent can guarantee visa approval — the decision rests with the embassy. What we guarantee is a complete, error-free application with all supporting documentation in the correct format. Most rejections come from incomplete or inconsistent documents, which we eliminate. We also brief you on what to say at the visa interview.

faqs.q: What is the financial requirement?
faqs.a: Varies by country. UK Student Route requires £1,334/month (London) or £1,023/month (outside London) for up to 9 months, held in your account for 28 consecutive days ending no more than 31 days before the application date. Canada needs CAD 20,635 for first year living expenses plus tuition. Australia needs AUD 24,505 (2024 update). USA requires you to demonstrate financial capacity at the interview rather than meeting a fixed number. Your Regional Representative will give exact figures for your case.

faqs.q: Do I need IELTS?
faqs.a: Most English-medium destinations require an English-proficiency test: IELTS (Academic for most), TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic, or Duolingo English Test for some institutions. UK requires a SELT (UKVI-approved test) specifically — typically UKVI IELTS or PTE Academic. We help you choose the right test and book it.

faqs.q: Do I need a TB test for the UK?
faqs.a: Yes. Pakistani applicants applying for UK Student Route MUST have a TB test from a UK-approved clinic in Pakistan before the application. Approved clinics are in Islamabad, Karachi, and Lahore. We book this appointment for you as part of the package.

faqs.q: Can my family come with me?
faqs.a: Depends on the destination and your level of study. UK Student Route allows dependants only for postgraduate research courses (PhD/MRes) or government-sponsored students (since 2024 rule change). Canada and Australia have generous family routes that allow spouses and dependent children. USA F-2 visa is for F-1 dependants but does not allow the spouse to work. We can advise based on your specific program.

faqs.q: What is SDS (Study Direct Stream) for Canada?
faqs.a: SDS is Canada's expedited study-permit programme for students from select countries including Pakistan. To qualify you need: a Letter of Acceptance from a DLI, IELTS 6.0+ in each band, payment of first-year tuition, a CAD 20,635 GIC (Guaranteed Investment Certificate) from a Canadian bank, biometric submission, and a medical exam. Target processing: 20 calendar days, much faster than the regular Study Permit route.

faqs.q: Which countries' visit visas do you process?
faqs.a: Saudi Arabia (e-Visa tourist + Umrah-eligible), UAE (30-day and 60-day tourist), Schengen (29 European countries — Germany, France, Italy, Spain, Netherlands, Portugal, Greece, Austria, Belgium, and 20 others), UK (Standard Visitor / Family), USA (B1/B2), Canada (TRV), Australia (subclass 600 visitor), Malaysia, Singapore, Turkey (e-Visa), Thailand.

faqs.q: How long does processing take?
faqs.a: Saudi e-Visa: 24–48 hours. UAE tourist: 3–5 working days. Schengen: 15–30 days standard. UK Standard Visitor: 3 weeks standard, 5 working days priority, 24 hours super-priority (additional fees apply). USA B1/B2: interview wait time is the bottleneck — currently 6–12+ months in Pakistan for new applicants at both Karachi and Islamabad consulates. Canada TRV: 2–3 weeks. Australia: 2–3 months. Apply as early as your travel dates allow.

faqs.q: Do I need an invitation letter for family visits?
faqs.a: Most destinations require one when visiting family — UK, Schengen, USA, Canada all do. Your host abroad sends a signed invitation letter along with proof of their immigration status (visa / residence permit / citizenship document), proof of their address (utility bill / tenancy agreement), and proof of relationship (birth certificate, marriage certificate, etc). We tell you exactly what is needed for each destination.

faqs.q: How much money should I show in my bank account?
faqs.a: Varies by destination. Common guidance: USD 5,000–10,000 minimum for Schengen / UK / Canada to demonstrate funds for your trip. USA looks at your overall financial profile and ties to Pakistan (job, family, property), not just bank balance. Saudi tourist e-Visa requires proof of accommodation + return ticket but has a lower bank requirement. Your Regional Representative will tell you the figure for your case.

faqs.q: Do I need travel insurance?
faqs.a: Mandatory for Schengen (minimum €30,000 medical coverage, valid across all Schengen countries for the visa duration). Recommended for UK, Canada, USA. Most other destinations do not require it but it is sensible. We coordinate insurance with reliable providers — typical premiums are PKR 1,500–4,000 for a 30-day trip depending on age and destination.

faqs.q: Can I get a multi-entry visit visa?
faqs.a: Many destinations offer multi-entry options: Saudi e-Visa is 1-year multi-entry by default. UAE has 60-day multi-entry and 5-year multi-entry options. Schengen offers multi-entry visas (up to 5 years for frequent travellers with a clean history). USA B1/B2 is typically 5-year multi-entry. UK Standard Visitor is up to 10-year multi-entry. We will recommend the right option based on your travel pattern.

faqs.q: What if I have been refused a visa before?
faqs.a: Past refusals must be disclosed on every future application — concealing them is grounds for permanent ban. We work with you to understand why the refusal happened (most are document-related, some are intent-related) and prepare a stronger re-application with the issues addressed. Refusal does not mean permanent block; many re-applications succeed once the underlying problem is fixed.

faqs.q: Which Gulf countries do you handle work visas for?
faqs.a: All six GCC countries: UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, and Oman. Each has its own visa process, attestation requirements, and timeline — we are familiar with all of them.

faqs.q: What is GAMCA medical?
faqs.a: GAMCA (Gulf Approved Medical Centres Association) is the network of medical centres approved by GCC governments to conduct pre-departure health checks for workers. Tests include TB chest X-ray, Hepatitis B and C, HIV, syphilis, malaria (some countries), pregnancy test for women, and general physical examination. Required for all GCC work visas. Results are uploaded directly into the Gulf country's labour system — you cannot work around this. We book your appointment at the nearest approved centre.

faqs.q: How long does the process take?
faqs.a: Typically 4–8 weeks from job offer to visa-in-hand. The slowest steps are document attestation (HEC takes 5–15 working days for normal service, 1–3 days for urgent; MoFA 3–7 days; embassy 5–10 days) and medical clearance. We run them in parallel rather than sequentially to compress the timeline. Some embassies have express services for an additional fee.

faqs.q: Do you find me a job?
faqs.a: No — we are a visa-processing agency, not a recruiter. You need an existing job offer from a Gulf employer to start the visa process. Once you have it, we handle everything else. If you do not yet have an offer we can refer you to licensed Pakistani recruitment agencies, but we do not place workers ourselves.

faqs.q: Do I need polio vaccination?
faqs.a: Yes for travel to Saudi Arabia (booster within 12 months of travel is required by Saudi authorities for Pakistani nationals). Strongly recommended for UAE and other GCC countries. We book this at any approved vaccination centre in Pakistan.

faqs.q: What educational documents need attesting?
faqs.a: Typically your highest qualification (matric, intermediate, bachelor, master, professional certificate, trade certificate, etc.). The chain is: original document → IBCC equivalence (if foreign-issued) → HEC (Higher Education Commission Pakistan) → MoFA (Ministry of Foreign Affairs Pakistan) → destination country embassy in Islamabad. For some trades and unskilled roles, only matric/intermediate is needed. We handle each step on your behalf.

faqs.q: Can I change employers in the Gulf?
faqs.a: Depends on the country and your visa type. Saudi Arabia introduced job-mobility reforms in 2021 that allow some workers to transfer employers without sponsor permission after a contract period. UAE allows transfer with a No-Objection Certificate (NOC) or after contract expiry. Qatar abolished the Kafala system in 2020 and now allows transfers without NOC in many cases. Each country has nuances — your Regional Representative can advise on options once you arrive.

faqs.q: What if my visa is rejected?
faqs.a: Visa rejections at the work-visa stage are most often due to: document mismatches (name spelling differences between passport and educational documents), incomplete attestation, medical issues flagged at GAMCA, PCC concerns (past record), or employer-side delays in submitting paperwork on their end. We work with you to fix the root cause and re-apply. Genuine medical-fitness issues are the only category we cannot work around — those require resolving the underlying condition first.
